title: The explicit relative section diagram and cone cocone
statement: For a small diagram of schemes D:I→Sch, a stage i and an A-valued étale sheaf G on D_i, construct a functor from (Over i)^op to presheaves on D_i.Etale whose j object is the section presheaf of (D_j→D_i)*G on the base changes of D_i-objects. Its maps are the canonical unit comparisons. For any cone c on D, the canonical comparisons to sections of (c→D_i)*G form a cocone.

source.place: Detailed proof paragraph 2: canonical inverse-image unit maps; categorical composition and pullback-pasting coherence.

proof.text: For composition, move the first pullback-pasting restriction across the second unit by presheaf naturality, then move the first coefficient composition isomorphism across that unit by sheaf naturality. Inverse-image associativity combines the two coefficient isomorphisms. The composite-unit equation combines the units, and pullback-pasting associativity cancels the remaining inverse pasting map. For identity, the unit for an identity scheme map and all other comparison factors are isomorphisms. Composition makes this map idempotent; cancel it to get identity. These laws give the diagram functor laws. Their composition formula and the cone equation give naturality of the cocone.

proof_origin.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 2: finite skeleton descent and finite-cochain section continuity; explicit categorical construction with Grothendieck coefficients.

mathlib_searches.query: Inverse image adjunction units commute with composition isomorphisms and pullback pasting for sections of sheaves
The adjunction unit gives a functorial map from sections of an inverse image to sections after another base change and the maps satisfy identity and composition laws

from.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 2: finite skeleton descent and section representatives
